title: Kept Amount of a Returned Flood Premium: Definitions and Worked Figures
content:
On a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts the kept amount of a returned flood premium is the quantity defined in the clauses below, read from the reserve's records on the handling date.

(a) The withdrawn flood term is the withdrawn flood insurance bill on file with the latest due date, which is the day that term began; the reserve's payment of it is the reserve's flood insurance payment made against that bill.

(b) The cancellation date is the due date of the latest paid flood insurance bill when that date is on or after the day the withdrawn term began, and otherwise the handling date. The days in force are the calendar days from the day the withdrawn term began to the cancellation date and the months in force are the whole calendar months between those dates, neither below zero.

(c) The unearned flood premium is the reserve's payment of the withdrawn term times the policy-year days, 365, less the days in force, divided by 365.

(d) The reserve period left is the plan's reserve months, as the plan matrix shows them, less the whole calendar months from the reserve's established date to the handling date, never below zero; the horizon of the flood refund review is that many whole months.

(e) The tax part of the flood refund need is the annual property tax on file times the horizon months divided by twelve; the insurance part is the annual hazard premium plus the annual flood premium on file, times the horizon months divided by twelve. The flood refund need is the tax part plus the insurance part plus the flood refund cushion, and the flood refund cushion is zero.

(f) The flood refund room is the flood refund need less the reserve balance, never below zero, and the flood refund excess is the unearned flood premium less the room, never below zero.

(g) A flood refund excess above zero that is at least the release floor of 50.00 is released to the borrower's side; a smaller excess stays in the reserve. The borrower's side keeps the whole released flood refund excess.

(h) The kept amount of a returned flood premium is the unearned flood premium less the part of the released excess the borrower's side keeps, rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

The reserve paid 730.00 for a flood term that began on 1 April; the bill is now withdrawn, and no paid flood bill falls due on or after 1 April. On a handling date of 1 July the cancellation date is 1 July, the days in force are 91, and the unearned premium is 730.00 times 274, divided by 365: 548.00. On file: tax 2,400.00, hazard 1,200.00, flood 720.00; take a reserve period left of 3 months. Tax part 600.00, insurance part 480.00, need 1,080.00.

| Balance | Room | Excess | Released | Kept amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 900.00 | 180.00 | 368.00 | 368.00 | 180.00 |
| 590.00 | 490.00 | 58.00 | 58.00 | 490.00 |
| 580.00 | 500.00 | 48.00 | none (below 50.00) | 548.00 |
